disposition_reason: Insect ecotoxicology; no human dietary exposure or food concentration data.

study.design: laboratory bioassays of honey bee gustatory response, sucrose responsiveness and survival after selenate, selenomethionine or methionine dosing
study.method: proboscis extension reflex assays; acute and chronic feeding at 0 to 6000 mg/L in 1 M sucrose

non_numeric_findings: Bees fed selenate were less responsive to sucrose; chronic selenate dosing raised mortality more than a single dose (Abstract).
Selenomethionine increased mortality only at the highest concentration (Abstract).
